data.title: Initialize go spike contract
data.context: Reusable repo-local agent workflow stack. Make go/go-auto/go-loop practical: route rough Viggo commands, create or repair repo-local .go state, execute autonomously inside safety gates, validate with tests, and document exact operator usage.
data.decision: Use repo-local .go vision, principles, epics, tasks, evidence, and go auto loop for this project.
consequences: Feedback becomes tasks
go auto can continue from repo state

data.title: Make go-auto executable through a run envelope
data.context: go auto must be control handoff, not only task-list output; Hermes needs machine-readable preflight, budget, stop, checkpoint, and result boundaries.
data.decision: go auto emits execution_policy and run_envelope; repo-local go-workflow-stack now owns its own .go vision, principles, tasks, evidence, and decisions.
consequences: Hermes can execute go auto with less chat inference
Future executor work can target the auto-run-result schema

data.title: Make go auto a command train, not a command suggestion
data.context: Viggo reports go auto is not autonomous enough: he still has to spam obvious follow-up commands that should be chained by the workflow.
data.decision: go auto must mean agent control handoff: inspect route/status, claim or create the next task, execute verification/build/recheck/finish loops, create same-scope follow-ups, and continue until done, blocker, or explicit budget. The stack should emit/enforce a command-train contract, and Hermes skills should execute it with tools rather than returning instructions for Viggo to run.
consequences: Future stack work prioritizes autonomous train execution, budgets, continuation checkpoints, and fewer user-triggered micro-commands.

data.title: Use a compact execution brief as the advice handoff
data.context: Long recommendations are useful for reasoning but unreliable as an execution contract and force repeated prompts.
data.decision: Persist a schema-validated compact execution brief containing the problem, chosen approach, bounded work units, acceptance, verification, non-goals, and recommendation provenance.
consequences: The Go command can create semantically scoped tasks from the brief and, when execution is authorized, immediately run them.

data.title: Versioned stakeholder delivery contract
data.context: Substantial .go assignments need a consistent output that non-technical stakeholders can understand without repository or GitHub access.
data.decision: Define go-workflow.delivery.v1 with mandatory summary, assignment, delivered scope, excluded scope, evidence summary, limitations, open points, next steps, release identity, disclosure class, and machine-readable provenance. Stakeholder narrative is rendered in HTML while provenance remains structured and independently hashable.
consequences: Every generated delivery is comparable and forwardable; HTML remains derived output and never replaces repo-local JSON or JSONL state.

data.title: Portable first and publication adapter second
data.context: Stakeholders may lack GitHub access and projects may not exist on GitHub while public hosting can create privacy and revocation risks.
data.decision: The mandatory output is a self-contained HTML file plus JSON manifest. Building is local and side-effect free. Publishing is a separate explicit command through adapters. Initial stack scope implements file output only and defines a publisher interface; link-public or controlled hosting is an opt-in extension.
consequences: Every project can deliver without external infrastructure; hosting credentials and public side effects cannot block report generation or happen implicitly.

data.title: Fail-closed delivery disclosure classes
data.context: Generated stakeholder reports can accidentally expose local paths, prompts, credentials, customer data, internal logs, or repository-only evidence.
data.decision: Every delivery declares public, link-private, or restricted. The generator scans all rendered and manifest text for secret-like keys, credential files, local home paths, raw prompts, and unapproved customer identifiers. Unknown or omitted disclosure defaults to restricted. Publication requires explicit disclosure and a clean scan.
consequences: Generation remains useful for private delivery while public publication fails closed instead of assuming repository evidence is safe to disclose.

data.title: Immutable assignment delivery releases
data.context: A large assignment needs a stable handoff while corrections and later work must remain auditable rather than silently replacing what was sent.
data.decision: Deliveries are created explicitly for an epic or selected task set. States are draft, released, and superseded. Release ids combine a semantic slug and monotonically increasing version. Released artifacts are immutable; corrections create a new version that may supersede an earlier release.
consequences: Recipients can refer to an exact delivery and later corrections preserve the historical record. Individual task completion alone does not automatically publish a report.

data.title: Editorial evidence-led stakeholder delivery
data.context: The generated report must be readable, printable, mobile-safe, and directly forwardable without looking like a generic SaaS dashboard or internal agent transcript.
data.decision: Use an editorial report composition with strong release identity, readable typography, restrained green accent, explicit delivered versus excluded scope, evidence rows, limitations, and disclosure notice. Avoid card stacking and repository-centric jargon in the visible narrative.
consequences: The renderer has a concrete visual contract and can be regression-tested against named sections and responsive overflow.

data.title: Require accepted governing decisions for consequential tasks
data.context: The released architecture lane can currently claim and finish material work when a brief defines quality attributes but neither the task nor its applicable briefs reference any decision. Viggo explicitly authorized closing this gap with Go after reviewing the trade-off.
data.decision: Every effectively material or foundational task must resolve at least one exact accepted governing decision from its task metadata or applicable accepted briefs. Reusing an existing governing decision is preferred; a new per-task ADR is not required when an accepted decision already governs the work.
consequences: Claim fails with an actionable missing-governing-decision finding when the combined reference set is empty.
Existing missing or non-accepted referenced decisions continue to fail closed.
None/local tasks and legacy repositories remain unaffected.

data.title: Bind v0.3.14 release validation to template commit 490dd506
data.context: The v0.3.14 annotated stack tag exists, and the canonical public template now adopts it at commit 490dd50671dd740e5902ad17ed475258bb7c939b. Release validation must stop consulting mutable template HEAD.
data.decision: Add an immutable 0.3.14 HTTPS pairing to template commit 490dd50671dd740e5902ad17ed475258bb7c939b while retaining the 0.3.13 mapping as historical provenance.
consequences: Canonical v0.3.14 validation is reproducible after future template changes.
Historical v0.3.13 validation remains reproducible.

data.title: Zelfstandige release als taak-eindvoorwaarde
data.context: A/B/C-onderzoek en expliciete planning-only opdracht; gewenste richting, nog geen geïmplementeerde garantie.
data.decision: Iedere nieuwe uitvoerbare producttaak levert een zelfstandig resultaat met volledige projectgebonden lifecycle. Bestaande done-taken, mechanical/no-diff werk en de smoke-fixture vereisen een expliciete compatibiliteitsgrens; geen verzonnen releases.
consequences: Taken blijven open en ongeclaimd; verduidelijk resterende beleidskeuzes voordat betrokken gedrag wordt vastgelegd.

data.title: Verse workers met repositorygebonden context als basis
data.context: A/B/C-onderzoek en expliciete planning-only opdracht; gewenste richting, nog geen geïmplementeerde garantie.
data.decision: Plan een vaste runner met verse workers per taak/fase en een contextsnapshot. Zelfde-sessie wissels en subagents blijven optionele adapters totdat abc-09 de capabilities en gewenste ondersteuning onderbouwt. Geen mid-turn hot-switch beloven.
consequences: Taken blijven open en ongeclaimd; verduidelijk resterende beleidskeuzes voordat betrokken gedrag wordt vastgelegd.

data.title: Expliciete modelkeuze zonder stille fallback
data.context: A/B/C-onderzoek en expliciete planning-only opdracht; gewenste richting, nog geen geïmplementeerde garantie.
data.decision: Plan projectdefaults met taak- en optionele critic-overrides, capabilitycheck en bevroren effectieve instellingen per run. Exacte defaultmodellen, automatische escalatie en live-accounttoegang zijn nog niet gekozen.
consequences: Taken blijven open en ongeclaimd; verduidelijk resterende beleidskeuzes voordat betrokken gedrag wordt vastgelegd.

data.title: Eén taakwerkplek met gecontroleerde integratie
data.context: 2026-09-13 user: Verwerk die oude inzichten; Go task; planning only
data.decision: Plan één branch/worktree per taak, één canonieke control state, veilige modeloverdracht, seriële integratie en revisiegebonden releasebewijs. Exacte naamgeving, integratiestrategie en testomgevingisolatie blijven projectkeuzes.
consequences: abc-11 levert werkplekbeheer; abc-03/04/05/06 integreren context, herstel en shipping. Legacy code dient als bron, niet als huidige runtimegarantie.

data.title: Zelfstandige release als taak-eindvoorwaarde
data.context: Prepared ABC direction authorized by user GO on Astra High; bounded implementation choices for abc-01.
data.decision: Introduce versioned opt-in execution contracts. Product work requires an explicit release profile; historical and unconfigured legacy tasks keep existing behavior. Mechanical/no-change work uses an explicit non-release profile with a reason. Source template smoke fixtures remain reusable and are not fake product releases. Product version, runtime version and task/run IDs remain distinct.
consequences: abc-01 implements contract validation and dependency gates; later ABC tasks implement dispatch/worktrees/publication. No additional public deployment rights are inferred from model selection.

data.title: Expliciete modelkeuze zonder stille fallback
data.context: User selected Astra High and authorized the ABC execution sequence; installed Codex model/list capabilities inspected.
data.decision: Freeze explicit task and optional critic selections at first execution. Query the installed Codex catalog before any worker writes; force runtime model and reasoning options. Introduce no implicit global model or automatic escalation. Keep effective identity unconfirmed unless authoritative runtime evidence exists. Hermes/custom controlled selection is unsupported until its adapter explicitly implements it; legacy commands remain usable.
consequences: No model quality/cost rankings or provider guarantees are inferred from a catalog response.

data.title: Eén expliciete taakwerkplek met canonieke control state
data.context: User authorized the prepared ABC/legacy execution sequence; one worktree per task and serial integration were the planned baseline.
data.decision: Require explicit workspace path, branch and base branch/commit. Bind registry and Git worktree marker to task/owner/run; resolve registered-worktree Go commands to canonical .go. Use existing process locks for creation, writing and serial integration. Refuse foreign paths, scope violations and unproven cleanup. No implicit branch heuristic, publisher, service-port or database policy.
consequences: Active-task orchestration and handoff consume these primitives in abc-03/04; cleanup never republishes.

data.title: Durable worker context verified against current state
data.context: abc-03 follows shipped task/model/workspace contracts; workers must continue without chat history.
data.decision: Create immutable per-dispatch snapshots in canonical .go with file/hash references and explicit phase feedback. Verify task, workspace, Git/index/worktree content and raw evidence before launch. Keep legacy inline environment behavior; opted-in tasks use bounded references and explicitly selected repo-local context.
consequences: Active resume and model topology remain abc-04/09; raw evidence and code remain authoritative.

data.title: Exclusive managed phase resume with explicit initial workspace
data.context: abc-04 follows verified model selection, owned workspaces and durable phase context; current loop cannot resume after a build exhausts its budget.
data.decision: Add an opt-in managed native phase runner with explicit initial workspace bindings, persisted phase/effect intent and completion, preserved model/context/requirements, and process-aware exclusive recovery. Resume from proven phase; invalidate affected proof after drift. Support explicit stopped-owner local relocation; do not infer cross-host quiescence or old checkpoint phases.
consequences: Release/deployment publishers remain abc-05/06/07; the managed runner exposes their intent/readback and cleanup recovery boundaries.

data.title: Require content-bound proof before opted-in completion
data.context: User GO authorizes abc-05 after v0.3.19; old finish-before-ship and prose-only evidence remain insufficient for self-contained product tasks.
data.decision: Apply one strict completion gate to current opted-in finish, approval and reporting. Capture declared local checks plus review and content identity, verify explicit Git-tag/GitHub-release readback, and keep unknown or failed shipping pending. Preserve historical done records/unconfigured legacy semantics under abc-d01; publisher/deploy automation follows in abc-06/07.
consequences: Read-only release verification is distinct from publication authority; no model-success or populated field can replace command and remote proof.

data.title: Publish configured task releases through durable intent and exact readback
data.context: User GO continues after abc-05 v0.3.21. Completion proof is enforced; the managed runner still stops at release_pending.
data.decision: Add an explicitly configured controller publisher for version preparation, final proof, scoped commit/integration, annotated tag and GitHub release. Bind task/run/owner, frozen profile and explicit push authority. Serialize publication, reconcile every interrupted effect by exact readback, reject stale bases/conflicting tags, and finish through the shared gate. Keep deployment and default migration in their existing later tasks.
consequences: Unconfigured profiles do not gain publication rights. Inconclusive remote results remain pending; owned workspaces and evidence survive retries. No GitHub Actions or silent force operations.

data.title: Require explicit target authority and authoritative live deployment proof
data.context: User GO continues after abc-06 v0.3.22 publication. Package/deployment providers remain project-specific onboarding inputs.
data.decision: Extend explicit release profiles with no-deployment policy or controlled package/deploy/readback argv adapters. Freeze target and separate deployment authorization; bind released commit/version and optional artifact hash. Require stable idempotency identity and authoritative absent/accepted/live/unknown observations. Retain pending state on inconclusive results and finish only through verified live proof. Use local fixtures and no real production target in this implementation.
consequences: Existing profiles remain release-only. New required deployments cannot use Git push permission as deployment authority. No automatic rollback, production data changes, GitHub Actions or provider selection.

data.title: Adopt lifecycle policy explicitly with recoverable state and preserved provenance
data.context: User GO continues after abc-07 v0.3.23. Existing project history and user-selected policies must remain distinguishable from new opt-in defaults.
data.decision: Add an explicit lifecycle configuration path to repository migration, separate from stack-pin/schema updates. Preview before apply, journal exact state for recovery/rollback, convert only eligible open records and preserve existing overrides/history. Reuse intake resolution and preserve full task/project contract provenance in non-executable review bundles.
consequences: No inferred model or shipping/deployment authority, no historic proof fabrication, no active-run transfer, no mandatory broad skill chain and no global skill mutations.

data.title: Verse workers met repositorygebonden context als basis
data.context: User GO; shipped owned workspace/context/resume baseline and locally inspected Codex 0.153.4 protocol. abc-09 will capture reproducible fixture proof; live baseline proof remains abc-10.
data.decision: Support fresh ephemeral native CLI workers at task/phase boundaries with frozen per-phase profiles, canonical context snapshots and one owned worktree. Defer persistent app-server turn/session adapters and subagent adapters: protocol capability exists but Go-specific ownership, recovery and attribution integration is not implemented. No mid-turn switch or implicit new worktree per model.
consequences: Deferred alternatives do not block the baseline. Any later adapter must prove exact session identity, explicit per-phase overrides, canonical recovery, exclusive writer and read-only critic. No chat transcript is the lifecycle source of truth.

data.title: Reuse explicit decision dependencies and content review for task readiness
data.context: Authorized task asks for minimum compatible readiness improvement. Audit found architecture claim returns early for none/local tasks before inspecting explicit governing references. Structural checks and process success do not judge semantic adequacy.
data.decision: Honor explicitly declared architecture scope/decision dependencies even at none/local impact, without requiring new metadata or conformance on unreferenced simple tasks. Retain existing material/foundational requirements. Strengthen repo-local authoring and native build/critic guidance with a source-grounded review disposition and matching requirement evidence. No new readiness boolean, keyword classifier, global skill change or approval system.
consequences: Unreferenced none/local tasks and legacy history remain unchanged; explicitly missing, draft or non-accepted governing dependencies prevent dependent claim and finish.
Research may examine unresolved choices within research-only scope; it must not declare the unresolved proposed rule as an accepted implementation prerequisite.
Routine delegated tuning stays autonomous. Unsupported bug-fix or requested-outcome claims remain pending/blocked through existing outcome and critic paths.

data.title: Bind serial campaigns to explicit authority and existing outcome proof
data.context: autonomy-01 defines the minimum campaign contract before dependent runtime work. Existing ABC task, workspace, completion and publication records remain authoritative. The autonomy-first plan prefers reliable serial progress and forbids unlimited work from vision.
data.decision: Use opt-in immutable go-workflow.campaign-contract.v1 revisions to bind original intent, adopted goal outcomes, canonical task R# text references, applicable vision/principles and exact accepted decisions. Bound execution with an explicit task allowlist, outcome-linked research/repair allowances, selected model profiles, shared budget, separate release/deployment grants and mandatory stops. Preserve unresolved material decisions and use existing delegation and architecture gates. No duplicate task queue or outcome status store.
consequences: Validation is read-only and cannot grant authority, prove completion or start a worker. Existing historical contracts are unchanged.

The serial controller must retain immutable revisions and cumulative consumption, validate current references, admit bounded expansion before execution and apply existing task/workspace/architecture/release gates.
An empty eligible queue stops with unresolved outcomes; only content-bound behavioral, critic and required delivery evidence can establish goal completion.
Parallel builders, a new approval system, implicit production destinations and GitHub Actions remain excluded.
